name: Commure Scribe
description: Commure Scribe is a well-funded ($820M+) AI medical scribe used by 75,000+ clinicians across 25M+ patient encounters annually. Pricing is transparent: $59/month billed annually ($89 monthly). 7-day free trial with no credit card required. Includes AI Copilot, custom templates, ICD-10/CPT coding suggestions, and support for 60+ EHRs with direct synchronization. Multi-language support (90+ languages). Commure acquired Augmedix in 2024 and has major enterprise partnerships including HCA Healthcare. Not built for mental health-specific documentation—therapists should use purpose-built tools.
short_description: Well-funded AI scribe at $59-89/mo. 75,000+ clinicians. 7-day free trial. 60+ EHR integrations. ICD-10/CPT coding. Multi-language (90+).

faqs.q: How much does Commure Scribe cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Commure Scribe Pro costs $59/month when billed annually ($708/year) or $89/month billed monthly. A 7-day free trial (Scribe Core) is available with no credit card required. Enterprise pricing is custom.

faqs.q: Does Commure Scribe have a free trial?
faqs.a: Yes. Scribe Core offers a 7-day unlimited trial with no credit card required. Includes in-person and telehealth support, 60+ language transcription, and multi-speaker recognition.

faqs.q: How many EHRs does Commure Scribe integrate with?
faqs.a: Commure Scribe integrates with 60+ EHR systems including Epic, Cerner (Oracle Health), athenahealth, and eClinicalWorks. Enterprise tier includes direct note synchronization.

faqs.q: Is Commure Scribe good for mental health?
faqs.a: No. Commure Scribe is designed for primary care and medical specialties. Therapists should use Mentalyc ($20-70/mo) or Upheal ($69/mo). Psychiatrists should consider Freed ($39-119/mo) or mdhub.

faqs.q: Commure Scribe vs Freed: which is better?
faqs.a: Both offer transparent pricing. Freed ($39-119/mo) is cheaper and better for solo practitioners. Commure ($59-89/mo) has more EHR integrations (60+) and multi-language support (90+ languages). Commure has more enterprise credibility ($820M+ funding, 75,000+ clinicians).
